mainTopic: Foods bought from non-Jews (fish roe, olives, locusts, apple wine) and the start of the new פרק on statues
overview: The גמרא finishes its talk about fish roe. It reads a ברייתא about egg-like signs as speaking of fish innards, such as the swim bladder. When no expert is around, רב יהודה trusts a seller who says 'I salted them,' while רב נחמן wants the seller to show the actual fish. Next the גמרא explains several items in the משנה's list: bits stuck to a חלתית leaf, soft olives softened by their own oil, and רבי יוסי's overripe olives whose pit slips out. A ברייתא teaches that food and apple wine taken from a non-Jew's storage are permitted, but goods sold out in the market may have wine added. A story tells how רבי was cured by seventy-year-old apple wine of non-Jews. רב ששת explains that a suspected כהן is trusted for his stored food, because he fears the חכמים. The פרק then ends, and a new משנה argues about which statues are forbidden. The גמרא explains this as a dispute over worrying about a minority, and limits it to statues of kings at a city's entrance.

steps.title: A ברייתא says fish roe has signs like eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier view by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say fish roe has kosher and non-kosher signs, just like bird eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: just as there are signs for eggs, so there are signs for fish roe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier view of רבי דוסתאי by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say fish roe must be checked by signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fish roe has signs just like eggs, then some fish roe must be non-kosher and needs checking. That clashes with the view that fish roe does not need this kind of checking.

keyTerms.meaning: The signs of eggs, which show whether an egg is kosher

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: like the signs of eggs,
phrases.notes: These are bird eggs. A kosher bird's egg has one round end and one pointed end.

phrases.english: so are the signs of fish roe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier view in the sugya about fish roe
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that fish roe does not need checking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives fish roe kosher signs like eggs, which means some fish roe is not kosher.

steps.title: The ברייתא is really about fish innards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא already had to be reinterpreted anyway, so it can be read as talking about fish innards instead of fish roe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't you yourself have to reinterpret that ברייתא? Read it as: so are the signs of fish innards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier view by rereading the ברייתא so that it talks about fish innards instead of fish roe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could not be read in its simple way anyway, so everyone already had to reinterpret it. Since it needs reworking regardless, the earlier view reads it as fish innards, and then the ברייתא says nothing about fish roe.

keyTerms.meaning: You had to reinterpret it (fix its reading) anyway

phrases.english: Didn't you have to reinterpret it?
[Read it:] so are the signs of fish innards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that fish roe needs signs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about fish innards, so it does not touch the question of fish roe.

steps.title: How can fish innards be round and pointed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: where would fish innards have the egg sign of being round on one end and pointed on the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: But where do you find that a sign of fish innards is being round and pointed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the answer from step 2. The egg signs are about shape, so how could they apply to fish innards?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs of an egg are its shape: one end round, the other pointed. Innards don't normally have that shape, so the new reading seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: And where do you find (such a case)?
Round and pointed, the shape of a kosher egg

phrases.english: But where do you find
among the signs of fish innards
that it should be round and pointed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reinterpretation given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as fish innards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Egg signs are about shape, and innards don't seem to have an egg shape.

steps.title: The swim bladder has an egg shape
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the egg-shape signs apply to the fish's swim bladder.
steps.simpleTranslation: You find it with the swim bladder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that one part of the innards, the swim bladder, really can be checked by the egg's shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The swim bladder is shaped like an egg, so the signs of round and pointed fit it. This makes the reading from step 2 work.

keyTerms.meaning: The swim bladder of a fish (an air sac shaped like an egg)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about egg signs is read as fish innards, and it fits the swim bladder, so it gives no proof about fish roe.

phrases.english: You find it with the swim bladder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No fish innards could have an egg shape.
steps.terutzMaskana: The swim bladder has an egg shape, so the reading holds.

steps.title: What if there is no expert?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is when no expert is available to tell whether the fish roe is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no expert there, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new practical question and sets up a disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the assumption was that someone could check the roe. Now the question is what to do when nobody can tell kosher roe from non-kosher roe.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert, here someone who can tell kosher fish roe apart

phrases.english: If there is no expert there, what [is the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the signs of roe to the practical case where no one can check
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether fish roe can be bought from a seller when no expert can check it

steps.title: רב יהודה: the seller's word is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that once the seller says 'I salted them,' the roe is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: once the seller says 'I salted them,' they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question: we can rely on the seller saying that he salted the fish himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller is claiming that he salted the fish this roe came from, and that they were kosher. For רב יהודה, that statement is enough to permit the roe even without an expert.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Once [the seller] says 'I salted them,' they are permitted.
phrases.notes: He means: I salted the fish this roe came from myself, and they were kosher fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller's statement 'I salted them' is enough to permit the roe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permitted once the seller says he salted them.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the seller must show the fish
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees and says the roe is permitted only when the seller says 'These are the fish and these are their innards.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: not until he says 'These are the fish, and these are their innards.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposing view and requires more than just the seller's general claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, a general claim is not enough. The seller must point to the actual kosher fish and connect the roe to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he says, meaning not permitted unless he says
Their innards, here including the roe inside them

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב יהודה and רב נחמן rely on the seller's words. The difference is whether a general claim is enough, or whether he must point to the actual fish.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
[It is not permitted] until he says
'These are the fish, and these are their innards.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permitted only when the seller identifies the actual fish the roe came from.

steps.title: רב יהודה ruled this way in practice
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב יהודה told his attendant אדא that once the seller says 'I salted them,' the roe is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה instructed אדא his attendant: once the seller says 'I salted them,' they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that רב יהודה actually followed his own ruling in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer just a theory. רב יהודה used his ruling as a real instruction to the person who did his shopping.

keyTerms.meaning: He instructed him (gave him a ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה: the seller's 'I salted them' is enough. רב נחמן: the seller must show the actual fish. רב יהודה ruled his way in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹרִי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לַאֲדָא דַּיָּילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda instructed Adda the attendant:
Once [the seller] says 'I salted them,' they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹרִי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לַאֲדָא דַּיָּילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב יהודה's ruling from step 6 put into practice
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה relied in practice on the seller saying 'I salted them.'

steps.title: The משנה: the leaf of חלתית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה's list of permitted foods: the leaf of חלתית.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] and the leaf of חלתית [is permitted].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the leaf of חלתית, a plant used as a spice or medicine, among the things that may be eaten when bought from a non-Jew. The next step will ask why this needed to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant used as a spice or medicine

phrases.english: And the leaf of chiltit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts discussing a new item from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leaf of חלתית is permitted.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to teach that the leaf is permitted, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for saying something that seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה forbade a piece of חלתית only because it may have been cut with a non-kosher knife. A leaf is never cut, so of course it is permitted. Why say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (asks why something needs to be taught)

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משנה quoted in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the leaf of חלתית is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only concern with חלתית is a non-kosher knife, and a leaf is not cut, so the ruling seems obvious.

steps.title: The pieces stuck to the leaf are also permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching about small pieces found on the leaf. We do not worry that a non-Jew mixed in cut pieces; they simply stuck to the leaf when it was picked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for the small pieces on it. You might have thought we should worry that he brought cut pieces and mixed them in. So the משנה teaches that they just stuck to it and came along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the new point of the משנה is about small bits found on the leaf, not the leaf itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small bits of חלתית on the leaf could look like cut pieces, so we might fear a non-Jew added pieces cut with his knife. The משנה teaches that we assume they just stuck on naturally when the plant was pulled up.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for (the case of)
Slipped or stuck on by itself

steps.whatToRemember: The leaf of חלתית is permitted, and so are the bits stuck to it. We assume they came along naturally and were not cut and added.

phrases.english: It is needed only for the small pieces on it.
You might have said: let us worry
that perhaps he brings [cut pieces] and mixes them in,
phrases.notes: He means pieces a non-Jew might have cut with a non-kosher knife.

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that this is a case of slipping on
that it stuck on and came along with it.
phrases.notes: The bits got caught on the leaf when the plant was pulled up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the משנה to a less obvious case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bits on the leaf might be cut pieces a non-Jew added, so they would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bits stuck on naturally, so they are permitted too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the משנה teaches something new: we do not invent a worry that a non-Jew mixed in cut pieces when there is a natural explanation.

steps.title: Quoting the next item in the list: rolled olive cakes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next permitted item, rolled olive cakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and rolled olive cakes are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next food on the משנה's list of permitted items. This sets up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are olives pressed together into a soft, round shape. The משנה lists them as permitted even when bought from a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Large, soft olives (named after a soft kind of bread)

phrases.english: And rolled olive cakes (are permitted).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the same משנה list, after the leaf of חלתית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rolled olive cakes bought from a non-Jew are permitted.

steps.title: Why is this not obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers to say that olive cakes are permitted. There seems to be no reason to forbid them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain olives have nothing forbidden in them. So a rule saying they are permitted seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משנה's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to say that rolled olive cakes are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason to suspect them, so saying they are permitted adds nothing.

steps.title: Very soft olives: softened by their own oil, not by wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for very soft olives. We might think wine was added to soften them, but the softness comes from their own oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed even when they are very soft. You might have said the non-Jew put wine in them. So the משנה teaches us that they softened because of their own oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about olives that are very soft. We do not suspect that wine made them soft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the olives are so soft, one might think a non-Jew soaked them in wine, which would make them forbidden. The משנה teaches that the softness comes from the olives' own oil, so there is no worry. This matches the pattern of step 11, where an unusual detail turns out to have an innocent cause.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a special case

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
even though they are very soft.
You might have said: he put wine in them,
so it teaches us:
these softened because of the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּרָפֵי טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case to one where a suspicion would arise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Very soft olives might have been softened with wine, so they should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The softness comes from the olives' own oil, so they are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוסי forbids overripe olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line in which רבי יוסי says overripe olives are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: overripe olives are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's opinion from the משנה. This sets up a question about what 'overripe' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי disagrees about one kind of olive, the שלחין. He forbids them, but the משנה does not yet say exactly which olives these are.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says: overripe (olives) are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with רבי יוסי's opinion on a kind of olive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, overripe olives are forbidden.

steps.title: What are overripe olives?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of שלחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are overripe olives like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which olives count as שלחין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a definition, not an attack. We need to know which olives רבי יוסי forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are overripe (olives) like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word שלחין used in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to identify the olives רבי יוסי forbids.

steps.title: An olive so soft that its pit slips out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says these are olives so soft that their pit slips out when you hold them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: any olive that, when you hold it in your hand, its pit slips out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא gives a simple test for overripe olives. If the pit slides out when you hold the olive, it is an overripe olive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is about how soft the olive is. Olives this soft are the ones רבי יוסי forbids.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
Any (olive) that, when one holds it in his hand,
its pit slips out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא כֹּל שֶׁאוֹחֲזוֹ בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Overripe olives are olives whose pit slips out when they are held.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about locusts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about locusts that come from different places.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: locusts that come (from a shopkeeper's basket are forbidden; from storage they are permitted).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה's line about locusts. This sets up a ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates locusts by where they come from. The ברייתא that follows spells out the details.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Locusts that come, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: locusts from a shopkeeper's basket are forbidden, and those from storage are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Locusts bought from a non-Jew depend on where they come from.

steps.title: A ברייתא: from storage they are permitted, sold in the market they are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says locusts, caper buds and leeks from a storehouse, storeroom or ship are permitted. Those sold in the market in front of the shopkeeper are forbidden, because he sprinkles wine on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: locusts, caper buds and leeks that come from the storehouse, the storeroom or the ship are permitted. Those sold in the market in front of the shopkeeper are forbidden, because he sprinkles wine on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה. Food that comes straight from storage is fine, but food set out for sale in the market is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jewish shopkeeper sprinkles wine on his goods so they may have absorbed non-Jewish wine. Food in bulk storage is not handled that way, so there is no worry.

keyTerms.meaning: The market, where goods are set out for sale

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the general idea in this section: the worry depends on how the seller usually handles the food.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Locusts, caper buds and leeks
that come from the storehouse,
from the storeroom, or from the ship are permitted.
Those sold in the market in front of the shopkeeper are forbidden,
because he sprinkles wine on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's line about locusts with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food from storage is permitted. Food sold in the market is forbidden because wine may have been sprinkled on it.

steps.title: The same rule for apple wine of non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the same rule to apple wine. From storage it is permitted, but in the shop it is forbidden because grape wine is mixed into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, apple wine of non-Jews that comes from the storehouse, the storeroom or the seller's basket is permitted. Apple wine sold in the market is forbidden, because they mix wine into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and applies the same idea to apple wine. This also sets up the story about רבי that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Apple wine is not grape wine, so by itself it is not a problem. The worry is that shopkeepers mix grape wine into it. Apple wine from storage does not raise that worry.
steps.confusionAlert: Apple wine is not forbidden in itself. The only worry is that grape wine was mixed into it.

phrases.english: And similarly, apple wine of non-Jews
that comes from the storehouse or from the storeroom
or from the seller's basket is permitted.
That which is sold in the market is forbidden,
because they mix wine into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the storage-versus-shop rule of step 19 to apple wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Apple wine of non-Jews from storage is permitted. In the shop it is forbidden because grape wine may be mixed in.

steps.title: רבי, with a stomach ache, asks about apple wine
steps.stepSummary: In a ברייתא, רבי has a stomach ache and asks if anyone knows whether apple wine of non-Jews is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: once רבי had a stomach ache. He said: is there anyone who knows whether apple wine of non-Jews is forbidden or permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about apple wine. רבי needs it for his stomach and asks whether he may drink it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי, the leader of his generation, does not know the answer himself. He wants a reliable ruling before drinking it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Once Rabbi felt pain in his stomach,
phrases.notes: "רבי" on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: he said: is there anyone who knows

phrases.aramaic: יֵין תַּפּוּחִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם אָסוּר אוֹ מוּתָּר?
phrases.english: whether apple wine of non-Jews is forbidden or permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story connected to the apple wine rule of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether apple wine of non-Jews is permitted.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי: my father drank it and was cured
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי tells how his father drank seventy-year-old apple wine of non-Jews and was cured.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי said before him: once my father had a stomach ache. They brought him seventy-year-old apple wine of non-Jews, and he drank it and was cured.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers with a story about his own father, רבי יוסי, which shows that this apple wine is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is a precedent: a great Sage actually drank apple wine of non-Jews. That shows the wine is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
Once my father felt pain in his stomach,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵבִיאוּ לוֹ יֵין תַּפּוּחִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם
phrases.english: and they brought him apple wine of non-Jews
that was seventy years old,
and he drank it and was cured.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A precedent: רבי יוסי drank apple wine of non-Jews, which shows it is permitted.

steps.title: רבי: you knew this and let me suffer!
steps.stepSummary: רבי complains that רבי ישמעאל had this information all along and let him suffer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: you had all this in your hand, and you made me suffer!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי reacts to the answer. He accepts it and complains that it was not told to him sooner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's reaction shows that he accepted the precedent as a valid ruling. The story ends with apple wine of non-Jews treated as permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Food and apple wine from a non-Jew's storage are permitted. Items from a shopkeeper's basket are forbidden because wine may have been added. רבי accepted the story of רבי יוסי as proof that apple wine of non-Jews is permitted.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, speaking to רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: You had so much in your hand,
and you made me suffer!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל כָּךְ הָיָה בְּיָדְךָ וְאַתָּה מְצַעֲרֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי's reaction to the answer in step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי accepts the precedent, so apple wine of non-Jews is treated as permitted.

steps.title: They find old apple wine, and רבי is cured
steps.stepSummary: They search and find a non-Jew with three hundred jugs of seventy-year-old apple wine. רבי drinks it, is cured, and thanks God.
steps.simpleTranslation: They checked and found one non-Jew who had three hundred big jugs of seventy-year-old apple wine. רבי drank and was healed. He said: Blessed is the Omnipresent, who handed His world over to keepers!
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי's stomach ache ends. They find the old apple wine, he drinks it, and he gets better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the story from steps 21–23. Because רבי drinks the non-Jew's apple wine, we see in practice that stored apple wine of non-Jews is permitted. His blessing thanks God for arranging that someone kept this wine for seventy years, ready for exactly this moment.

keyTerms.meaning: the Omnipresent, a name for God

steps.whatToRemember: Stored apple wine of non-Jews is permitted, and רבי himself drank it to be healed.

phrases.english: They checked and found one non-Jew

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי יַיִן
phrases.english: who had three hundred large jugs of wine
of apples, seventy years old,
and he drank and was healed,
He said: Blessed is the Omnipresent
who handed His world over to keepers!
phrases.notes: He means God made sure someone kept this wine all those years, so it would be there when he needed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story that began with רבי's question in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Old stored apple wine of non-Jews was used by רבי, which shows it is permitted.

steps.title: What does 'and the same for תרומה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'and the same for תרומה' and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the same for תרומה.' What does 'and the same for תרומה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a short phrase in the משנה and asks what it means. This sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'the same,' without saying who or what case it is talking about. The גמרא needs to work out how the rule about storehouses and shops applies to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy portion of produce given to a כהן; non-כהנים may not eat it

phrases.english: And the same for תרומה.
What is 'and the same for תרומה'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the apple-wine story and goes back to explain another phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does 'and the same for תרומה' refer to, and how does the rule apply to it?

steps.title: A suspected כהן is trusted for food from his storage
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains: a כהן suspected of selling תרומה as ordinary food is distrusted only for food in front of him. Food from his storehouse is permitted, because he is afraid the חכמים will find out and make him lose his goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The same applies to a כהן who is suspected of selling תרומה as ordinary food. Only what is in front of him is forbidden. But what comes from the storehouse, the storeroom or the basket is permitted. He is afraid. He thinks: the חכמים will hear about me and make me lose it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. A suspected כהן is treated like the shopkeeper in steps 19–20: the food right in front of him is a problem, but his stored food is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the כהן sells cheaper תרומה and calls it ordinary food. רב ששת limits the suspicion to food that is right in front of him. Food in his storage is trusted, because selling תרומה in a large, public way could get back to the חכמים, and he would lose his business.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the same pattern found throughout the section. Suspicion applies to small amounts close at hand, not to large stored supplies where cheating would be risky and easily exposed.

phrases.english: רב ששת said:
And the same for a כהן who is suspected
of selling תרומה as ordinary food,
it is only what is in front of him that is forbidden,
but what comes from the storehouse
or from the storeroom or from the basket is permitted,
because he is very afraid,
he thinks: the Rabbis will hear about me
and make me lose it.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, others the word in square brackets. Either way it means 'and they will make me lose it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase refers to a כהן suspected of selling תרומה as ordinary food. Only the food in front of him is forbidden, while his stored food is permitted, because he fears the Rabbis.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אין מעמידין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of פרק אין מעמידין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'אין מעמידין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is finished. This is the traditional goodbye line said at the end of every פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line does not teach any law. It marks the end of the פרק and expresses the hope of coming back to learn it again.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'אין מעמידין.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the last discussion.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: all statues are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: רבי מאיר says all statues are forbidden, because they are worshipped at least once a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All statues are forbidden, because they are worshipped once a year. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. רבי מאיר rules that you may not benefit from any statue at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason is that statues are worshipped at least once a year. So we assume any statue was made for עבודה זרה, even if nothing on it shows that.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden' here means it is forbidden to get any benefit from the statue. It is not only about worshipping it.

phrases.english: משנה: All statues are forbidden,
phrases.notes: This means you may not benefit from them, for example by selling them.

phrases.english: because they are worshipped
once a year,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, it is forbidden to benefit from any statue.

steps.title: חכמים: only statues holding a staff, bird or ball are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say only a statue holding a staff, a bird or a ball is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: The only statue that is forbidden is one that has in its hand a staff, a bird or a ball.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר and narrow the rule. Only statues with certain objects in their hand are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, a statue is not automatically assumed to be an idol. Holding one of these three objects is a sign that it was made for worship, so only those statues are forbidden.

phrases.english: And the חכמים say:
Nothing is forbidden except any statue
that has in its hand a staff
or a bird or a ball.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר and narrows which statues are forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a statue holding a staff, a bird or a ball is forbidden.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a statue holding anything is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that a statue holding any object at all is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even any statue that has anything at all in its hand is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל widens the חכמים' list, so a statue holding any object is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the חכמים that a plain statue is not forbidden. But for him, any object in the statue's hand is a sign of worship, not only the three objects the חכמים listed. His view falls between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions about statues. רבי מאיר says all statues are forbidden. The חכמים say only those holding a staff, a bird or a ball. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says any statue holding any object.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ כׇּל דָּבָר.
phrases.english: Even any statue that has anything at all in its hand is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the חכמים' list of objects that make a statue forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A statue holding any object at all is forbidden.

steps.title: If statues are worshipped yearly, why do the חכמים permit them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by challenging the חכמים: if statues are worshipped once a year, how can they permit them?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If the statues really are worshipped once a year, what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and pushes on the חכמים. רבי מאיר gave a reason, that statues are worshipped once a year, so how can the חכמים permit them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason sounds like a fact. If it is true, the statues are עבודה זרה and should be forbidden. So the חכמים seem to have no answer, and the גמרא wants to know how they could disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
If they are worshipped once a year,
phrases.notes: This is quoting רבי מאיר's reason from the משנה (step 28).

phrases.english: what is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּנֶעֱבָדִין פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה by questioning the חכמים' position against רבי מאיר's stated reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of the חכמים in the משנה (step 29)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר's fact is true, statues are worshipped and should be forbidden, so the חכמים' leniency seems to have no basis.

steps.title: Only one town worshipped statues; the dispute is about worrying for a minority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that statues were worshipped yearly only in רבי מאיר's town. רבי מאיר worries about a minority and forbade them everywhere; the חכמים do not, so they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In רבי מאיר's town they worshipped statues once a year. רבי מאיר, who worries about a minority, made a גזירה on other places because of that place. The רבנן, who do not worry about a minority, did not make a גזירה on other places because of that place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: statues were not worshipped everywhere, only in רבי מאיר's own town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the argument is not about a fact. It is about a rule: should we forbid something everywhere because a small minority of places use it for idol worship? רבי מאיר says yes, as a גזירה; the חכמים say no.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is really about חשש למיעוטא: רבי מאיר forbids all statues because of one town's practice; the חכמים do not.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying that every statue everywhere is actually worshipped. He knows it happened only in his town, but he forbade all of them as a גזירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a disagreement that looked like a fact into a known halachic principle about whether we worry about a minority.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
In the place of Rabbi Meir

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ עוֹבְדִין אוֹתָהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: they would worship it once a year,
and Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for a minority,

phrases.aramaic: גָּזַר שְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת אַטּוּ אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: decreed on other places because of that place,
and the Rabbis, who are not concerned for a minority,

phrases.aramaic: לָא גָּזְרוּ שְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת אַטּוּ אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: did not decree on other places because of that place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 by limiting רבי מאיר's fact to one town.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the fact and moving the dispute to a principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Statues are worshipped everywhere once a year, so the חכמים seem to have no reason to permit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי מאיר's town worshipped them; the dispute is whether to forbid other places because of a minority.

steps.title: The dispute is only about statues of kings
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the מחלוקת of the משנה to statues of kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: We learned this about statues of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל tells us which statues the משנה is talking about: statues of kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every statue is in the argument. Only statues of kings, which were sometimes worshipped, are where רבי מאיר forbids and the חכמים permit.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
We learned it regarding statues of kings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּאִנְדְּרָטִי שֶׁל מְלָכִים שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the dispute to defining which statues it covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת in the משנה is only about statues of kings.

steps.title: And only statues standing at the city entrance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a further limit: the statues in the מחלוקת are ones standing at the entrance to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: And we learned this about statues standing at the entrance of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows the case even more: the statues must stand at the city's entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A statue placed at an important spot like the city gate is more likely to be worshipped. So only there does רבי מאיר forbid; the word "and" shows this is added on top of שמואל's limit.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's מחלוקת is only about statues of kings that stand at the entrance to a city.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And we learned it regarding those standing at the entrance of the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּבְעוֹמְדִין עַל פֶּתַח מְדִינָה שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second condition to שמואל's definition of the case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only to statues standing at the entrance of the city.
